Good evening lounge crew,
Route planning, this evening: a short note from our desk

Please keep companion-animal files moving in the ledger as soon as service changes land. Clear notes help the whole team act fast, and they keep the handoff clean between check-in, cabin support, and the safety coordinator. If a traveler arrives with a concern, keep the tone steady, check the record, and pass only the facts we need for the next step. We are better when the desk works as one crew, and our guidance should stay concise, kind, and actionable.

For claim handling, use the standard intake path and attach the supporting record before the file moves on. <<FACT F117>> If the case also touches a missed connection, route that note through the same file so the review stays in one place. <<FACT F110>> Keep language plain in the ledger, avoid loose phrasing, and make sure the final note reflects what was confirmed, not what was assumed. That is especially important when a traveler is worried about a pet in transit, because a calm, accurate update saves time for everyone.

A quick reminder from the Companion Animal Travel Desk at Aurelia Skyways: send any unresolved service change to the lead on duty before you close out the shift. If Gus, or any other pet case, is already in motion, make sure the chain of custody is complete and the traveler has the next contact point. Thanks for staying alert, keeping the notes clean, and supporting each other through the evening push.

Companion Animal Travel Desk
